title: A spectral map is continuous for the constructible topologies
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a spectral map: $f$ is continuous and $f^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Y$. Then $f$ is continuous as a map from $X$ with its constructible topology to $Y$ with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (on each space, the topology with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets and their complements): for every subset $A\subseteq Y$ open in the constructible topology of $Y$, the set $f^{-1}(A)$ is open in the constructible topology of $X$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2S (label lemma-fibres-spectral-map-quasi-compact, line 4373), part (1) ('follows immediately from the definitions'); used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2W (line 4810)

proof.text: *Step 1 (subbasic opens of the first kind).* Write $X'$, $Y'$ for $X$, $Y$ with their constructible topologies [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open subset. Since $f$ is continuous, $f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $X$; since $f$ is spectral, $f^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact. So $f^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-compact open subset of $X$, hence a member of the subbase of the constructible topology of $X$, hence open in $X'$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2S (label lemma-fibres-spectral-map-quasi-compact, line 4373), proof of part (1): 'follows immediately from the definitions'; definitions in Definition Tag 08YG (label definition-spectral-space, line 4276) and the paragraph after it (line 4290)

proof.text: *Step 2 (subbasic opens of the second kind).* Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open subset. Then $f^{-1}(Y\setminus W)=X\setminus f^{-1}(W)$, and $f^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-compact open subset of $X$ by Step 1. So $f^{-1}(Y\setminus W)$ is the complement of a quasi-compact open subset of $X$, a member of the subbase of the constructible topology of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology], hence open in $X'$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2S (label lemma-fibres-spectral-map-quasi-compact, line 4373), proof of part (1): 'follows immediately from the definitions'; definitions in Definition Tag 08YG (label definition-spectral-space, line 4276) and the paragraph after it (line 4290)

proof.text: *Step 3 (conclusion).* The topology of $Y'$ is the topology generated by the collection $\mathcal{B}$ of the quasi-compact open subsets $W\subseteq Y$ and their complements $Y\setminus W$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. By Steps 1 and 2, $f^{-1}(B)$ is open in $X'$ for every $B\in\mathcal{B}$. Hence $f:X'\to Y'$ is continuous [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-iff-subbase], applied to the topological space $X'$, the set $Y$ and the collection $\mathcal{B}$; that is, $f^{-1}(A)$ is open in $X'$ for every $A\subseteq Y$ open in $Y'$. (The hypothesis that $X$ and $Y$ are spectral [def-weil-spectral-space] is not used beyond the definition of a spectral map.)
